Execute only the approved bounded action, then reconcile its result with authoritative product state.
Show a receipt or clear local-only result and provide a refusal, retry, revoke, or alternative path.
lessons.analogy: A travel assistant may prepare the address and explain the route, but you still decide whether to open the map, share your location, or hand over a document from your bag.
nextjs: Keep device APIs inside client components reached through explicit visible controls; perform capability detection and render a meaningful alternative before requesting permission.
Validate files by size, declared and detected type, count, and purpose; show upload progress separately from local selection and use signed, narrow destinations.
Represent agent suggestions as inert typed intents. Only a genuine user event can invoke clipboard, picker, download, navigation, camera, or location behavior.
python: Issue short-lived upload or action tokens scoped to session, tenant, object type, maximum size, content purpose, and expiry; revalidate at ingestion.
Quarantine and scan uploaded artifacts where the risk requires it, strip unnecessary metadata, and do not trust browser MIME declarations.
Return durable artifact IDs and processing receipts rather than exposing storage paths, infrastructure credentials, or raw internal exceptions.

caseStudy.situation: The Acme agent asks Maya to upload a customer letter and use her location to choose a regional policy.
walkthrough: The interface explains that location is optional and offers manual region selection, so Maya chooses the manual path.
A real file picker opens only when Maya presses Choose letter; no file is read beforehand.
Maya previews the filename, type, size, fields to redact, upload destination, retention, and purpose.
After confirmation, the server scans and stores the file, returns an artifact receipt, and the UI links that exact version to the review.
caseStudy.result: Maya completes the task while refusing one permission and knowingly approving the minimum necessary file disclosure.
caseStudy.danger: A friendly agent message can become coercive if the browser prompts unexpectedly, refusal breaks the workflow, or a generic device tool can reach arbitrary files and destinations.
caseStudy.takeaway: The agent proposes; the host explains; the user gestures; the browser mediates; the server revalidates; the receipt proves the result.

lessons.lab: Specify clipboard, file upload, download, open-link, camera, and location tools. For each, document user activation, browser permission, purpose, preview, data flow, refusal alternative, server revalidation, cancellation, error, privacy, and receipt.
lessons.checkpoint: May an agent call a browser file picker automatically after writing 'Please upload a file'?
lessons.answer: No. The product should present a clear control and let a genuine user gesture invoke the picker. The message is a proposal, not permission or activation.
glossary: User activation - browser-recognized human interaction required for some capabilities
Frontend tool - typed device or browser action mediated by the host
Local-first - processing data on the device before optional disclosure

lessons.title: Interface security, data exposure, and safe rendering
lessons.stability: Web security standards evolve; maintain threat models, dependency updates, browser tests, and defense in depth
lessons.diagramPrompt: Show UNTRUSTED INPUTS MODEL TEXT RETRIEVAL TOOL RESULT APP MESSAGE URL FILE entering ENCODE, SANITIZE WHERE NEEDED, SCHEMA, ORIGIN, CSP, PERMISSIONS POLICY, SANDBOX, AUTHZ, REDACTION. Safe outputs TEXT COMPONENT LINK DOWNLOAD. Coral XSS DATA LEAK PROMPT SPOOF CLICKJACK CONFUSED DEPUTY blocked and logged.
lessons.alt: Untrusted model text, retrieval, tool results, app messages, URLs, and files pass encoding, schema, origin, policy, sandbox, authorization, and redaction controls before safe components render; common web attacks are blocked.
lessons.outcome: Apply ordinary web security and agent-specific trust boundaries to every dynamic interface input and action.
lessons.explanation: Model output, retrieved documents, tool results, MCP App messages, filenames, URLs, and generated component payloads are untrusted input. Fluency, an internal source, or a signed-in user does not make content safe to execute. Contextual output encoding is the default defense for text. Sanitization is needed only when the product intentionally supports a limited markup language, and the sanitizer configuration becomes security-critical. Avoid raw HTML whenever structured components can express the same meaning. CSP limits where scripts, frames, styles, images, and connections may come from. Permissions Policy limits powerful browser features. Iframe sandboxing restricts embedded code. These controls overlap but do not replace validation, authorization, or safe component design. Data minimization happens before rendering. A component should receive only fields it needs, at the correct tenant and purpose, with secrets, hidden prompts, chain-of-thought, credentials, raw policy internals, and unrelated customer data removed. Every action must be authorized on the server using current identity, tenant, resource, policy, revision, and approval—not trusted because a hidden field, React state, iframe, or model message says it is allowed. Security failure needs a safe interface state. Block the node or action, preserve unaffected work, show a plain support reference, and log a redacted diagnostic. Never dump the malicious payload or stack trace into the page.
trace: Inventory every interface input, renderer, frame, bridge, browser capability, action endpoint, data field, and external destination.
Classify trust boundaries and apply schema, size, encoding, URL, origin, content, and tenant rules before the component layer.
Use strict CSP, restrictive frame and permissions policies, secure cookies, anti-CSRF controls, and server-side authorization appropriate to the architecture.
Test stored and reflected XSS, malicious Markdown, unsafe links, oversized trees, spoofed approvals, cross-tenant IDs, forged app messages, and clickjacking.
Render bounded recovery, rotate or revoke exposed authority, preserve evidence, and convert every incident into a regression case.
lessons.analogy: A mailroom treats every package as unopened and potentially unsafe. A familiar return address may guide routing, but it does not bypass scanning, recipient checks, or access-controlled delivery.
nextjs: Keep secrets and privileged data in Server Components or server modules; pass client components minimal serialized view models rather than database records or provider responses.
Render text as text, allow links only after scheme and destination policy, avoid dangerous HTML sinks, and configure CSP with nonces or hashes rather than broad unsafe directives.
Reauthorize every Server Action and route handler, bind actions to current resource revisions, and treat client-supplied role, tenant, price, approval, and artifact fields as assertions to verify.
python: Centralize tenant-scoped authorization and redaction before response serialization; use explicit response models so accidental fields do not leak.
Validate URLs, content types, bridge methods, component schemas, identifiers, and size limits at ingress, and use safe libraries rather than custom parsers.
Create security fixtures for hostile retrieved text, tool outputs, app messages, and uploads, then run them through API, renderer, and browser tests as one end-to-end story.

caseStudy.situation: A retrieved policy contains hidden markup designed to create a fake Acme approval button and send customer data to an external URL.
walkthrough: Retrieval returns the content as untrusted evidence text, not as UI code.
The component renderer encodes the markup, and link policy blocks the unapproved destination.
CSP prevents unexpected script and connection sources even if a future renderer mistake occurs.
The security event receives a redacted correlation reference, the legitimate evidence remains available, and the payload becomes a permanent regression fixture.
caseStudy.result: The malicious document cannot impersonate product controls or exfiltrate customer data, and Maya can continue with the safe evidence.
caseStudy.danger: Agent systems widen the input surface: one unsafe renderer can turn model, RAG, tool, or embedded-app content into code or a believable fake control.
caseStudy.takeaway: Treat every dynamic source as data, expose the minimum, authorize effects on the server, and layer browser defenses around mistakes.

lessons.lab: Threat-model a generated comparison screen from source to browser. Add at least twenty abuse cases covering XSS, unsafe URLs, data overexposure, forged actions, cross-tenant access, iframe messages, CSP bypass, clickjacking, downloads, denial of service, and misleading consent. Define prevention, detection, recovery, and regression evidence.
lessons.checkpoint: If CSP blocks inline scripts, may the application safely render arbitrary model HTML?
lessons.answer: No. CSP is defense in depth and has limits and configuration risks. Arbitrary HTML can still spoof controls, leak data through allowed channels, abuse links, or exploit a future mistake. Prefer typed components and contextual encoding.
glossary: Contextual encoding - escaping data for its exact HTML, attribute, URL, or script context
CSP - browser policy restricting content sources and execution
Confused deputy - privileged component tricked into using its authority for an untrusted requester

lessons.title: A reusable visual lesson content model
lessons.stability: The content model is a product contract; version it independently from the website framework
lessons.diagramPrompt: Show AUTHORING SOURCE feeding VALIDATED LESSON MODEL with OUTCOME, STATUS, DIAGRAM, ALT, EXPLANATION, TRACE, ANALOGY, NEXTJS, PYTHON, CASE STUDY, LAB, CHECKPOINT, GLOSSARY, SOURCES, LINKS. Outputs DOCX WEBSITE SEARCH OFFLINE QUIZ. Add SCHEMA VERSION MIGRATION and coral COPY PASTE DRIFT.
lessons.alt: One validated, versioned lesson model containing the complete visual teaching structure produces the document, website, search, offline package, and quizzes while preventing copy-and-paste drift.
lessons.outcome: Design one durable lesson source that can power documents, a website, search, accessibility, and future learning experiences.
lessons.explanation: The website should not begin by copying paragraphs out of Word files. A structured content model becomes the source of truth, while DOCX, web pages, search records, offline packs, quizzes, and future formats become projections. Each lesson needs a stable ID and slug, module, title, learning outcome, standards status, diagram asset, alt text, detailed explanation, visual trace, analogy, technology mappings, case study, lab, checkpoint, glossary, relations, and cited sources. Stable identifiers matter more than filenames. A title or URL can change without breaking progress, bookmarks, annotations, prerequisites, citations, analytics, and links if the lesson ID remains stable. The schema needs a version and migration policy. Additive optional fields are easier than silent meaning changes. A migration should preserve author intent, report information loss, and leave a reversible record of what changed. Content and presentation are separate but connected. The model stores semantic roles and relationships; templates decide typography, layout, breakpoints, and interaction. Do not store visual spacing as a pile of HTML fragments inside lesson text. Validation belongs in authoring and CI. Missing alt text, unknown source labels, broken relations, duplicate IDs, unbounded prose, absent case-study fields, or unsupported diagram formats should block publication before learners see them.
trace: Define stable course, module, lesson, source, term, checkpoint, and asset identities plus explicit relationships.
Create a versioned JSON Schema or equivalent typed model with required semantic fields and bounded content rules.
Validate authoring input, cross-references, accessibility equivalents, URLs, assets, and source freshness before building.
Generate DOCX, web routes, search documents, offline manifests, feeds, and quiz payloads from the same validated snapshot.
Store the content version and build receipt with every published artifact so a learner or editor can reproduce it.
lessons.analogy: A well-organized kitchen keeps ingredients in labeled containers and uses recipes for different meals. Copying a finished casserole to make soup is fragile; starting from the same ingredients and recipe data is repeatable.
nextjs: Validate course JSON during the build, generate static lesson routes from stable slugs, and derive navigation, metadata, structured data, source panels, and related lessons from the same object.
Keep rich prose in a controlled Markdown or portable-document AST field if needed, with a strict renderer and semantic components rather than arbitrary MDX execution.
Emit contentVersion and schemaVersion into page metadata and cache tags so corrections can invalidate exactly the lessons and indexes that changed.
python: Model the schema with Pydantic, including validators for unique IDs, module membership, source references, related-lesson existence, alt text, and complete case studies.
Build deterministic exporters for JSON, DOCX input, search records, glossary indexes, and offline manifests from one immutable course snapshot.
Write explicit migrations from each supported schema version, test round trips, and retain an audit report of changed, defaulted, or dropped fields.

caseStudy.situation: Maya corrects one explanation and adds a new source. In the old workflow she must update the DOCX, website, search index, and quiz notes separately.
walkthrough: Maya edits the lesson source once and increments the content revision, not the stable lesson ID.
Validation confirms the source label exists, the relation graph is valid, and every accessibility field remains complete.
The build regenerates the lesson page, document section, source register, search record, and offline manifest from the same snapshot.
A receipt lists changed outputs and content hashes, while unchanged lessons remain cached.
caseStudy.result: Every format presents the same corrected lesson, and the team can prove which source produced it.
caseStudy.danger: Copying content between formats creates silent differences, stale citations, missing alt text, broken checkpoints, and corrections that reach only some learners.
caseStudy.takeaway: One semantic lesson model, many verified projections, stable IDs, explicit versions, and no copy-and-paste publishing.

lessons.lab: Create a JSON Schema for one Volume 9 lesson and three valid fixtures. Add twenty invalid fixtures covering IDs, relations, sources, alt text, empty arrays, oversized fields, unsafe rich text, wrong module, missing case-study fields, and future schema versions. Define a v1-to-v2 migration.
lessons.checkpoint: Should the DOCX file itself be the database for the future website?
lessons.answer: No. Keep a structured, versioned semantic source and generate both DOCX and website from it. A document can remain a polished deliverable without becoming the canonical data model.
glossary: Content model - typed structure and relationships describing learning material
Stable ID - identity that survives title and URL changes
Projection - output generated from the same authoritative content snapshot

lessons.title: Responsive diagrams, zoom, annotations, and reading order
lessons.stability: WCAG 2.2 and semantic web patterns are stable baselines; test actual assistive technologies and device layouts
lessons.diagramPrompt: Show one VISUAL LESSON adapting to DESKTOP TABLET MOBILE ZOOM 400%. Layers OVERVIEW, NUMBERLESS FUNCTIONAL LABELS, HOTSPOTS, ANNOTATIONS, PAN ZOOM RESET, KEYBOARD, READING ORDER, ALT TEXT, DETAILED EXPLANATION. Coral TINY TEXT, HORIZONTAL TRAP, COLOR ONLY, IMAGE OF TEXT. Teal EQUIVALENT PATH.
lessons.alt: One visual lesson adapts across desktop, tablet, mobile, and 400 percent zoom with keyboard zoom and pan, annotations, clear reading order, alt text, and a detailed equivalent explanation; tiny text and color-only meaning are rejected.
lessons.outcome: Make complex diagrams usable at every screen size and through visual, keyboard, zoom, and screen-reader paths.
lessons.explanation: A large diagram and a small phone screen cannot share one fixed viewing assumption. Responsive design may scale the overview, change the surrounding layout, and offer deliberate zoom and pan while keeping controls and explanations outside the image usable. The diagram is one representation of the lesson, not the only representation. Concise alt text states the purpose and overall relationship; the detailed explanation and trace provide an equivalent learning path without trying to squeeze an essay into alt text. Annotations should connect a hotspot to a stable concept, not pixel coordinates alone. Store normalized positions or semantic node IDs, keep annotation order explicit, and recalculate visible placement as the asset resizes. Keyboard users need focusable controls for zoom in, zoom out, reset, next annotation, previous annotation, and perhaps directional pan. Focus must remain visible and the viewport must not trap normal page scrolling. Reading order is authored. A screen reader should encounter the outcome, overview, diagram alternative, detailed trace, and controls in a coherent order. CSS positioning must not create a different semantic sequence. Visual quality includes contrast, non-color cues, readable functional labels, adequate target sizes, reduced-motion behavior, high-resolution assets, and a reliable full-screen or new-window view without losing learner position.
trace: Start with the learning outcome and define the smallest set of visual relationships the diagram must communicate.
Author concise alt text, a complete textual trace, node or region metadata, annotation order, and any long description.
Render a responsive overview plus explicit zoom, reset, annotation navigation, and full-screen controls with native semantics.
Test 320 CSS pixels, landscape and portrait, 200 and 400 percent zoom, reflow, keyboard, touch, screen readers, reduced motion, and high contrast.
Preserve the learner's selected annotation and scroll position when the layout, route, or offline state changes.
lessons.analogy: A museum map has a wall overview, a handheld version, clear symbols, a numbered audio tour, and staff explanations. Shrinking the wall map until the words disappear is not a mobile strategy.
nextjs: Use a semantic figure with external caption and explanation, responsive intrinsic dimensions, and a client viewer only for zoom, pan, and annotation state.
Keep diagram files free of lesson numbers and long titles; render those as HTML headings and captions so they reflow, localize, and remain accessible.
Store annotation coordinates and semantic order in lesson data, announce selected annotations concisely, and respect prefers-reduced-motion during viewport transitions.
python: Validate every diagram's dimensions, opaque background, filename, byte size, alt text, explanation, and annotation references during the content build.
Generate a contact sheet and automated image inventory for editorial review while preserving the original source PNG bytes in the published asset set.
Run link and relation checks that ensure every hotspot target exists and every diagram has a nonvisual equivalent before publication.

caseStudy.situation: Maya opens the event-driven interface diagram on a phone at 400 percent zoom and cannot read its functional labels in the first prototype.
walkthrough: The lesson switches to a single-column layout with a large overview and controls below the caption.
Maya opens the zoom viewer, uses keyboard controls, and moves through annotations in the authored logical order.
Each annotation has a short explanation linked to the matching node, while normal page scrolling remains available.
Maya can also skip the image and learn from the outcome, alt summary, visual trace, analogy, and case study in the same order.
caseStudy.result: The visual remains valuable without making the visual channel mandatory or forcing Maya to fight the viewport.
caseStudy.danger: A technically responsive image can still be inaccessible if labels become unreadable, pan traps scrolling, focus disappears, hotspots lack names, or important meaning exists only in color.
caseStudy.takeaway: Preserve the visual overview, add purposeful navigation, and provide an equally complete semantic learning path.

lessons.lab: Prototype one diagram viewer and test it at five viewport sizes, 200 and 400 percent zoom, keyboard only, touch, two screen readers, reduced motion, and forced colors. Record focus order, annotation order, scroll behavior, label readability, and the nonvisual equivalent.
lessons.checkpoint: Should the detailed diagram explanation be placed entirely inside the image alt attribute?
lessons.answer: No. Alt text should concisely identify the purpose and core relationship. Put the full trace and explanation in visible structured content so everyone can use it and navigate it.
glossary: Reading order - semantic sequence in which content is understood
Annotation - explanation tied to a visual node or region
Reflow - content adapting without two-dimensional scrolling for ordinary reading

lessons.title: Glossary, citations, search, prerequisites, and cross-links
lessons.stability: Search implementation is product-specific; source currency and prerequisite truth require ongoing editorial ownership
lessons.diagramPrompt: Show COURSE KNOWLEDGE GRAPH with LESSON nodes linked by PREREQUISITE, RELATED, BUILDS ON, CASE STUDY, TERM, SOURCE. SEARCH box applies QUERY, FILTER VOLUME MODULE TOPIC STACK STATUS, returns SNIPPETS with WHY MATCHED. SOURCE cards show OFFICIAL, CHECKED DATE, VERSION, SUPPORTS CLAIM. Coral BROKEN LINK STALE SOURCE CIRCULAR PREREQUISITE.
lessons.alt: A course knowledge graph connects lessons, terms, sources, prerequisites, related concepts, and case studies; transparent search filters results and source cards expose version and freshness while stale or broken relationships are flagged.
lessons.outcome: Turn many visual lessons into a navigable body of knowledge rather than a long folder of isolated pages.
lessons.explanation: A course becomes easier to learn when relationships are explicit. Prerequisite means knowledge required first; related means useful nearby material; builds on means a stronger conceptual dependency. These labels should not be collapsed into one vague More like this list. The glossary gives each term one stable identity, plain definition, aliases, first-use link, lessons that use it, and version notes where protocols disagree. Inline definitions help beginners without forcing constant page changes. Citations should connect a lesson claim to an authoritative source label, direct URL, checked date, relevant specification version, and status such as stable, candidate, or project-specific. A source register is not enough if readers cannot tell which lesson used it. Search needs lexical matching for exact terms and may add semantic retrieval for plain-language questions. Results should show why they matched, the lesson outcome, volume and module, standards status, and prerequisite warnings. Filters support different journeys: topic, protocol, technology stack, difficulty, artifact type, volume, module, status, lab, and case study. Search analytics must not become an excuse to collect raw private queries forever. A validation job should detect broken source links, unknown terms, orphan lessons, circular prerequisites, links to future unavailable material, duplicated definitions, and sources past their review date.
trace: Create stable records for lessons, terms, sources, topics, technologies, and relation types.
Validate the prerequisite graph as a directed acyclic learning path while allowing ordinary related links in both directions.
Build lexical and optional semantic indexes from approved public lesson fields, never from hidden author notes or private learner data.
Rank and explain results with outcome, matching passage, filters, status, freshness, and prerequisite context.
Schedule link, version, freshness, orphan, duplicate, and graph-integrity checks and route failures to an editorial queue.
lessons.analogy: A library needs more than shelves. The catalog, subject headings, cross-references, edition records, and a librarian's explanation help a beginner find the right book in the right order.
nextjs: Generate term, source, and topic indexes at build time; provide URL-addressable filters and server-rendered result summaries that work without client JavaScript.
Use a search endpoint that returns result ID, outcome, safe snippet, match reason, status, prerequisites, and source freshness rather than raw internal vectors or scores alone.
Render source links with direct destinations, checked dates, versions, and external-link cues; keep cross-links typed and accessible instead of relying on color or hover.
python: Build normalized search documents from the validated course model, with separate fields and weights for title, outcome, glossary, explanation, technologies, and sources.
Validate graph cycles, orphan nodes, duplicate slugs, missing reverse relations where required, URL health, source review dates, and unsupported source labels in CI.
If embeddings are used, version the model and index, retain lexical fallback, test known beginner queries, and expose an understandable match explanation.

caseStudy.situation: Maya searches 'how do I stop an agent after it already sent money' without knowing the words compensation or point of no return.
walkthrough: Semantic and lexical retrieval find the cancellation and compensation lesson using the plain-language explanation and glossary aliases.
The result says why it matched and distinguishes cancel, undo, and compensate before Maya opens it.
The page recommends the approval and authoritative-state prerequisites and links directly to the RFC and risk sources used.
Maya follows a typed Builds on path to the product-operations capstone without losing her original search filters.
caseStudy.result: Maya learns the right vocabulary and sequence even though she did not know the protocol or product-design term beforehand.
caseStudy.danger: Opaque semantic search can return an advanced or stale lesson with no explanation, while a flat keyword search can miss the learner's everyday language entirely.
caseStudy.takeaway: Model the knowledge relationships, explain search matches, expose source status, and guide beginners through prerequisites deliberately.

lessons.lab: Create a graph for Volumes 8 and 9 with all lessons, terms, sources, and at least four relation types. Write twenty beginner queries and expected results, including synonyms and misconceptions. Add tests for cycles, orphans, broken sources, stale versions, unsafe snippets, empty results, and privacy-safe query logging.
lessons.checkpoint: Are Related and Prerequisite interchangeable relationships?
lessons.answer: No. A prerequisite says the learner should understand something first; related material is useful but not required. The interface and graph validation should preserve that difference.
glossary: Knowledge graph - typed entities and relationships supporting navigation
Lexical search - matching words and phrases
Semantic search - matching meaning using a representation such as embeddings

lessons.title: Progress, checkpoints, quizzes, accessibility, and offline use
lessons.stability: Service Worker, IndexedDB, and Web App Manifest standards are current; offline behavior still varies by browser and storage policy
lessons.diagramPrompt: Show LEARNER choosing START LESSON, CHECKPOINT, QUIZ, LAB, BOOKMARK, NOTE. LOCAL PROGRESS and OPTIONAL SYNC merge through CONSENT and CONFLICT RULES. SERVICE WORKER caches APP SHELL CONTENT VERSION DIAGRAMS. OFFLINE badge leads to QUEUED ACTIONS then RECONNECT. Accessibility gates KEYBOARD SCREEN READER REFLOW REDUCED MOTION. Coral LOST PROGRESS STALE ANSWER SILENT SYNC.
lessons.alt: Learner progress, checkpoints, quizzes, bookmarks, notes, optional consented sync, and accessible controls work through an offline cache and reconnect queue with conflict rules, avoiding lost progress, stale answers, or silent synchronization.
lessons.outcome: Design a learning experience that preserves progress, supports practice, remains accessible, and behaves honestly offline.
lessons.explanation: Progress should represent meaningful learner actions, not time on page. Distinguish opened, viewed, checkpoint attempted, checkpoint understood, lab attempted, quiz completed, and learner-marked complete rather than manufacturing one percentage. Checkpoints give immediate retrieval practice; quizzes measure a broader set of outcomes; labs produce evidence of application. Explanations should teach after an answer and allow retry without shame, tricks, or dark-pattern streak pressure. Progress can begin locally with no account. If cloud sync is offered, explain the benefit, data fields, retention, devices, conflict policy, and deletion. Let the learner export and continue without consenting to analytics or personalization. Offline support needs a versioned shell, lesson content, diagrams, glossary, and source metadata. The product must label what is available offline and which links, dynamic searches, or source checks require a connection. Queued writes need idempotency and conflict rules. A bookmark is easy to merge; two edited notes may require both versions; a quiz answer must remain tied to the content and question version it answered. Accessibility covers the entire practice loop: answer controls, validation messages, explanations, score summaries, progress visuals, timers, drag alternatives, offline banners, synchronization conflicts, and saved-state announcements.

Store essential local progress in IndexedDB or an appropriate local store and make account sync optional and consented.
Precache a bounded versioned offline pack, report storage and freshness, and remove obsolete caches safely after activation.
Queue idempotent offline changes with timestamps and base versions, then reconcile explicitly after reconnect.
Test learning, assessment, conflicts, deletion, export, and recovery across keyboard, screen readers, zoom, reduced motion, offline, and constrained storage.
lessons.analogy: A paper workbook works anywhere, shows your pencil marks, and does not erase answers when the library closes. A digital course should preserve that confidence while adding optional synchronization and feedback.
nextjs: Render lesson and checkpoint fundamentals on the server, then progressively enhance local progress, notes, offline installation, and synchronization in isolated client components.
Use a versioned service worker strategy that precaches the shell and selected course packs, verifies content hashes, and shows explicit offline and update-ready states.
Key local records by stable content and activity versions; merge only safe fields automatically and surface note or answer conflicts with understandable choices.

Keep progress, quiz attempts, notes, consent, and analytics in separable data domains with export and deletion workflows that can be verified.
Generate signed course manifests listing offline assets and hashes, and test installation, partial download, quota failure, stale packs, upgrade, rollback, and cache cleanup.

caseStudy.situation: Maya downloads Volume 9 before a flight, completes two lessons offline, changes a note on two devices, and reconnects later.
walkthrough: The offline banner names the installed content version and explains that external standards links cannot be checked until reconnect.
Checkpoints, diagrams, glossary, and saved progress work without a network, while actions awaiting sync are visibly queued.
The server accepts idempotent lesson progress and presents both note versions instead of silently choosing the latest timestamp.
Maya merges the note, sees a sync receipt, and can export or delete all learner data from one privacy control.
caseStudy.result: Maya learns continuously without losing work or unknowingly sending data, even when connectivity and devices change.
caseStudy.danger: A decorative offline icon can hide stale content, broken source links, lost answers, duplicate submissions, silent account sync, and inaccessible conflict dialogs.
caseStudy.takeaway: Offline is a complete state model: version what is cached, preserve learner work, reconcile explicitly, and keep consent and accessibility intact.

lessons.lab: Design an offline pack and synchronization protocol for four lessons. Include asset manifest, content versions, quota failure, cache update, local progress, notes, quiz attempts, idempotency, two-device conflicts, optional account sync, export, deletion, accessibility, and twenty reconnect tests.
lessons.checkpoint: May the course silently upload locally stored notes when a learner later creates an account?
lessons.answer: No. Explain what will sync, obtain an informed choice, minimize the data, provide a local-only option, and make export, revocation, and deletion available.
glossary: Offline pack - versioned set of application and course assets available without a network
Idempotency key - identifier making a repeated mutation safe to recognize
Progress evidence - specific learning action rather than an invented engagement percentage

lessons.title: Asynchronous return, notifications, and attention management
lessons.stability: Notifications require permission and platform support; product attention policy remains application-specific
lessons.diagramPrompt: Show USER STARTS LONG TASK then LEAVES. DURABLE RUN continues through STAGES. RETURN OPTIONS IN APP BADGE, EMAIL DIGEST, PUSH NOTIFICATION behind USER CHOICE, URGENCY, QUIET HOURS, RATE LIMIT, PRIVACY, DEEP LINK. States READY NEEDS INPUT FAILED EXPIRED. Coral NOTIFICATION STORM, SECRET IN PREVIEW, FALSE URGENCY. Teal RESUME CONTEXT.
lessons.alt: A durable task continues after the user leaves and returns through consented in-app, digest, or push notifications filtered by urgency, quiet hours, rate limits, and privacy, with a deep link restoring context.
lessons.outcome: Let long-running agent work release the user's attention and call it back only when the timing and reason are genuinely useful.
lessons.explanation: A long task should not hold Maya hostage to an open tab. The product stores a durable run, explains what can continue, and lets her leave while preserving a clear way to return. Notifications are an attention budget, not proof that the system is alive. Useful reasons include a decision that blocks progress, completion of a requested deliverable, a recoverable failure, or an expiry that truly matters. Token updates and every tool call do not deserve interruption. Channel choice belongs to the user. In-app inbox, badge, email digest, browser push, or no external notification should have separate consent, urgency, quiet hours, frequency, preview-privacy, and revocation settings. A notification contains the minimum safe preview. Customer names, policy details, secrets, health or financial facts, and sensitive outcomes may appear on a lock screen or shared device, so the deep link should reveal protected detail after authentication. Deep links restore context: task identity, current authoritative stage, preserved artifacts, decisions needed, expiry, last seen position, and recovery choices. They must not encode authority or sensitive data in the URL. Deduplication and escalation rules prevent storms. Group related updates, suppress obsolete messages, acknowledge when the user returns, and never label ordinary product engagement as urgent.
trace: Classify task transitions as silent, inbox, digest, interruptive, or prohibited using user value and risk.
Apply channel consent, capability, quiet hours, rate limits, deduplication, locale, and privacy before delivery.
Create a minimal notification that names the task and required next step without exposing sensitive content.
Open an authenticated deep link that loads current authoritative state rather than replaying the stale notification body.
Record delivery, replacement, acknowledgement, expiry, revocation, and user preference changes as privacy-minimized receipts.
lessons.analogy: A good hotel concierge does not knock every minute to say work is continuing. They contact you at the agreed time when the room is ready or when a real decision cannot wait.
nextjs: Build an authenticated task inbox as the reliable return surface; treat push or email as optional pointers whose links resolve current state on the server.
Store notification preferences by channel, category, quiet hours, locale, and privacy level, and check them again at send time rather than at task creation only.
Use the Notifications API only after an understandable user request, and render permission-denied and unsupported states without blocking the underlying task.
python: Emit domain notification candidates from durable task transitions, then let a policy worker group, deduplicate, schedule, suppress, or deliver them idempotently.
Keep channel adapters separate from business events, use opaque deep-link identifiers, short expiries where appropriate, and server-side authorization on return.
Track delivery outcome and user acknowledgement without storing sensitive message bodies longer than necessary; honor revocation before queued delivery.

caseStudy.situation: Maya starts a forty-minute policy comparison, closes her laptop, and asks to be notified only if a decision is needed or the report is ready.
walkthrough: Acme persists the run and confirms that research can continue while Maya is away.
Intermediate tool and stage events remain in the task record but do not generate notifications.
A decision request arrives during quiet hours, so it waits in the inbox because its expiry is safely after quiet hours.
Maya returns through a minimal notification and sees current evidence, proposal version, remaining time, preserved artifacts, and all response choices.
caseStudy.result: The task progresses without occupying Maya's attention, and Acme interrupts only within the boundaries she selected.
caseStudy.danger: Notification storms, false urgency, sensitive lock-screen previews, and stale deep links can turn a helpful asynchronous agent into a distracting or privacy-invasive product.
caseStudy.takeaway: Durable work earns the right to wait; explicit attention policy earns the right to interrupt.

lessons.lab: Create an attention matrix for twenty task events across inbox, badge, digest, email, and push. Define consent, urgency, quiet hours, grouping, deduplication, expiry, preview privacy, deep-link state, unsupported behavior, revocation, and accessibility. Simulate a storm and prove suppression works.
lessons.checkpoint: Should every successful tool call send a notification so the user knows the agent is active?
lessons.answer: No. Tool events belong in the task record. Notify only for user-valuable transitions under the person's channel, urgency, quiet-hour, privacy, and frequency choices.
glossary: Attention policy - rules deciding whether and how a product may interrupt
Deep link - URL restoring a specific authenticated product context
Notification candidate - domain event proposed for delivery but not yet approved by channel policy

lessons.title: Privacy controls, consent, memory settings, and deletion
lessons.stability: Privacy obligations vary by jurisdiction and context; this course teaches product architecture, not legal advice
lessons.diagramPrompt: Show DATA LIFECYCLE COLLECT USE STORE SHARE REMEMBER EXPORT DELETE. USER CONTROL CENTER has PURPOSE, DATA CATEGORIES, MEMORY OFF SESSION PROJECT LONG TERM, RETENTION, CONNECTED APPS, DOWNLOAD, DELETE. CONSENT RECEIPT versions policy. DELETION FAN OUT to PRIMARY, VECTOR, CACHE, LOG, BACKUP SCHEDULE with VERIFICATION. Coral DARK PATTERN, BUNDLED CONSENT, GHOST MEMORY.
lessons.alt: A privacy control center explains data purposes, categories, memory scopes, retention, connected apps, export, and deletion; consent is versioned and deletion propagates through primary stores, vectors, caches, logs, and backup schedules with verification.
lessons.outcome: Give people understandable control over what an agent collects, remembers, shares, exports, and deletes across the complete data lifecycle.
lessons.explanation: Agent memory is a product data feature, not a magical property of the model. Session context, project facts, personal preferences, retrieved documents, summaries, embeddings, logs, and provider records are different stores with different purposes and risks. Consent must be specific enough to choose. Separate what is necessary to complete the current request from optional long-term memory, product analytics, model improvement, third-party sharing, notifications, and device synchronization. Memory controls should show the remembered item, source, purpose, scope, creation and last-use dates, expiry, who can use it, and a way to edit, forget, or pause future use. An off switch must affect retrieval and new writes, not merely hide the settings page. Deletion is a workflow. Primary records may feed object storage, vector indexes, caches, search, analytics, audit logs, downstream processors, and backups. The product needs a propagation map, exceptions, time bounds, retry, failure handling, and a verifiable status. Some audit or security records may need limited retention, but the interface should distinguish deletion, de-identification, legal hold, backup expiry, and inaccessible archival state rather than claiming everything vanished instantly. Data controls must resist dark patterns. Decline and delete should be as understandable as accept and save; choices must not be bundled, repeatedly nagged, hidden behind jargon, or punished with unnecessary loss of core function.
trace: Inventory every collected field, derived value, memory item, embedding, artifact, log, provider, purpose, retention, and recipient.
Separate necessary processing from optional purposes and capture versioned, revocable consent receipts for each optional category.
Expose memory and connected-app controls using the same identities and scopes enforced by write and retrieval paths.
Orchestrate export and deletion across all derived stores with idempotent steps, retry, exception reasons, and visible progress.
Verify that deleted or disabled data no longer appears in retrieval, personalization, search, sync, notifications, analytics, or future agent context.
lessons.analogy: A labeled filing cabinet tells you which drawer holds what, why it is kept, and who has a key. Shredding the index card while photocopies remain in five rooms is not deletion.
nextjs: Build one privacy center with server-rendered current settings, granular forms, clear consequences, accessible confirmations, export progress, and a durable deletion status page.
Do not put raw memory or consent decisions in unsigned client storage as authority; revalidate scope, policy version, and user identity on the server.
Render provenance and last-use information for memory items, and provide edit, forget, pause, export, and revoke controls without relying on prechecked boxes or asymmetric button styling.
python: Model consent as immutable versioned grants and revocations scoped to purpose, data categories, recipient, subject, product, policy version, and expiry.
Centralize memory retrieval behind a policy check and write a deletion saga covering source rows, documents, embeddings, caches, indexes, providers, and scheduled backup expiry.
Produce a user-facing completion receipt and internal exception evidence, then run retrieval probes that prove deleted items no longer influence answers.

caseStudy.situation: Maya turns off long-term personalization and asks Acme to forget a customer note that has already been embedded and included in a cached summary.
walkthrough: The control center identifies the source note, memory scope, embedding index, cached summary, retention, and downstream provider status.
Acme immediately blocks the item from new retrieval and starts an idempotent deletion workflow across primary and derived stores.
A failed cache purge retries without reopening access, while the interface reports partial completion and the affected system.
Verification probes confirm that future searches and agent context exclude the note; the receipt explains the backup-expiry schedule and any narrowly retained audit record.
caseStudy.result: Maya's choice changes actual memory behavior across the system instead of merely changing a toggle label.
caseStudy.danger: Ghost memory appears when a source record is deleted but embeddings, caches, summaries, provider data, or copied artifacts continue influencing the agent.
caseStudy.takeaway: Privacy control is enforceable data lineage: specific purpose, visible scope, revocation, propagated deletion, and verification.

lessons.lab: Draw a data inventory and lineage map for one agent conversation through prompts, messages, artifacts, memory, vectors, logs, analytics, providers, exports, and backups. Specify consent, retention, access, revocation, deletion steps, failure recovery, exceptions, completion receipt, and five proof probes.
lessons.checkpoint: Is deleting the primary database row enough to say an agent has forgotten the information?
lessons.answer: No. Derived embeddings, caches, summaries, indexes, copied artifacts, provider records, analytics, and backups must follow a documented deletion or expiry policy, and retrieval behavior should be verified.
glossary: Purpose limitation - using data only for the stated allowed reason
Consent receipt - versioned record of a specific informed choice
Ghost memory - deleted source data that survives in a derived or downstream store

lessons.title: Product analytics, feedback, evaluation, and experiment ethics
lessons.stability: Measurement design and experiment policy are context-specific; all course numbers are illustrative unless explicitly measured later
lessons.diagramPrompt: Show USER OUTCOME feeding PRODUCT EVENT, FEEDBACK, QUALITY EVAL, SAFETY REVIEW, ACCESSIBILITY EVIDENCE. METRIC CARD includes DEFINITION, NUMERATOR, DENOMINATOR, EXCLUSIONS, SLICE, WINDOW, VERSION. EXPERIMENT gate CONSENT, RISK REVIEW, FAIR ALLOCATION, STOP RULE, GUARDRAIL, DEBRIEF. Coral DARK PATTERN, VANITY METRIC, HIDDEN HARM, EXAMPLE AS FACT.
lessons.alt: User outcomes connect to minimized product events, feedback, quality evaluation, safety review, and accessibility evidence; every metric exposes its definition and denominator, while experiments require consent, risk review, fair allocation, stop rules, guardrails, and debriefing.
lessons.outcome: Improve an agentic product with honest evidence while protecting learners and users from manipulative measurement and unsafe experiments.
lessons.explanation: Product analytics asks what people did in the interface; evaluation asks how well the system performed on defined cases; feedback asks what people report; research explores why. They can inform one another but should not be merged into one satisfaction score. Every metric needs an operational definition, numerator, denominator, exclusions, eligibility, time window, content and software versions, and meaningful slices. Completion rate can be harmful if completion includes accidental approvals or excludes people who could not operate the interface. Collect the minimum events needed for a stated decision. Prefer semantic events such as approval reviewed or recovery completed over raw clickstreams, keystrokes, prompt contents, disability inference, or full session replay. Feedback controls should accept praise, confusion, incorrect content, accessibility barriers, privacy concerns, and safety incidents. Preserve the lesson, evidence, model, policy, and interface versions needed to reproduce the issue without demanding sensitive data. Experiments require risk classification. Cosmetic ordering may be low risk; approval language, disclosure, accessibility, privacy, pricing, notification urgency, or safety controls can materially affect people and deserve review, consent or exclusion, guardrails, and early stop rules. Ethical learning means publishing negative evidence, checking disparate impact and accessibility slices, avoiding coercive streaks or false urgency, documenting decisions, and never presenting hypothetical course metrics as measured product results.
trace: Start with a product decision and user outcome, then define the smallest evidence that could responsibly support it.
Write metric semantics, denominator, exclusions, slices, retention, access, and known failure modes before instrumentation.
Connect privacy-minimized product events with controlled evaluations, qualitative feedback, accessibility evidence, and incident records.
Review experiment risk, consent, allocation, guardrails, sample sufficiency, stop rules, rollback, and affected groups before exposure.
Publish results with uncertainty, negative findings, version manifest, practical effect, ethics review, and follow-up actions.
lessons.analogy: A teacher should not judge a lesson only by how many students reached the last page. They also examine understanding, barriers, skipped questions, different student needs, and whether the test itself was fair.
nextjs: Create a small typed analytics vocabulary from meaningful product transitions; redact payloads at the server boundary and disable optional analytics until the proper choice is recorded.
Build feedback forms that attach stable lesson, content, diagram, experiment, and interface versions while making free-text details optional and warning against sensitive information.
Resolve experiment assignment on a trusted server, expose a debug receipt to authorized staff, preserve accessibility, and include an immediate kill switch and deterministic fallback.
python: Define metric specifications in code or versioned configuration with event eligibility, numerator, denominator, exclusions, dimensions, minimum sample rules, privacy class, and owner.
Join product events to evaluation and feedback through opaque IDs and controlled access rather than copying raw conversations into an analytics warehouse.
Run slice, missingness, duplicate, allocation, guardrail, and rollback checks; label synthetic and illustrative datasets so they cannot be mistaken for observed performance.

caseStudy.situation: Acme considers changing an approval button from Review and approve to Continue because a prototype shows more task completions.
walkthrough: The team sees that completion alone rewards speed and may hide accidental approval, so it defines informed decision quality and cancellation as guardrails.
Risk review flags the vague Continue label as a material consent change and excludes it from an ordinary growth experiment.
Accessible moderated research and controlled evaluation show that the explicit label improves consequence understanding despite one extra second of review.
Acme keeps the understandable control, publishes the negative conversion result, and tests safer improvements to the decision summary instead.
caseStudy.result: Evidence improves comprehension without manipulating Maya into a faster but less informed decision.
caseStudy.danger: Optimizing clicks or completion can reward deceptive labels, inaccessible flows, notification pressure, privacy overcollection, and hidden harm to smaller groups.
caseStudy.takeaway: Measure decisions, not motion; combine analytics with evaluation and human evidence; experiment only within an explicit ethical boundary.

lessons.lab: Write a measurement plan for the visual course website with six outcomes, twelve minimized events, metric definitions and denominators, consent and retention, accessibility slices, feedback taxonomy, evaluation joins, three experiment risk classes, guardrails, stop rules, rollback, and a statement marking every sample number as illustrative.
lessons.checkpoint: If an experiment increases task completion, is it automatically a product improvement?
lessons.answer: No. Completion may rise through confusion, coercion, accidental approval, inaccessible exclusion, or privacy pressure. Examine understanding, safety, accessibility, recovery, user control, and practical effect with clear denominators.
glossary: Operational definition - exact rule turning observations into a metric
Guardrail - measure that must remain acceptable during change
Dark pattern - interface designed to manipulate a choice against the person's interests

lessons.title: Capstone: Acme Agent Workspace and Learning Platform
lessons.stability: Design capstone using the checked 2026-08-25 baseline; pin protocol versions and revalidate before implementation
lessons.diagramPrompt: Show two connected product zones AGENT WORKSPACE and VISUAL LEARNING PLATFORM. Inputs NEXTJS REACT FASTAPI MCP A2A AG-UI MCP APPS A2UI RAG TOOLS. Center HUMAN CONTROL LOOP REQUEST, PLAN, PROGRESS, EVIDENCE, PROPOSAL, APPROVAL, ACTION, RECEIPT, RECOVERY. Learning loop VISUAL, EXPLANATION, CASE, LAB, CHECKPOINT, PROGRESS. Cross-cutting ACCESSIBILITY SECURITY PRIVACY OBSERVABILITY EVALUATION OFFLINE. Coral STALE POLICY UNSAFE UI EXPIRED APPROVAL DATA LEAK blocked.
lessons.alt: The Acme capstone connects an agent workspace and visual learning platform through human-control and learning loops, using Next.js, React, FastAPI, MCP, A2A, AG-UI, MCP Apps, A2UI, RAG, and tools under shared accessibility, security, privacy, observability, evaluation, and offline controls.
lessons.outcome: Combine the full visual course into an implementation-ready product specification without prematurely writing the Next.js or Python project.
lessons.explanation: The capstone is one coherent product with two experiences. The Agent Workspace helps Maya complete governed customer work; the Visual Learning Platform teaches her how the protocols, evidence, decisions, and controls operate through the same visual course structure. Next.js and React own the web shell, accessible views, event reducer, diagrams, embedded app host, local learning state, and user controls. FastAPI owns typed APIs, durable work coordination, authorization, policy, consent, notifications, content validation, and export or deletion workflows. MCP connects agents to declared tools, resources, prompts, and optional Apps. A2A coordinates task-oriented peer agents. AG-UI carries typed interface events. A2UI can describe catalog-bound interface structure. RAG grounds answers in versioned evidence. None of these protocols replaces product identity, authorization, policy, or receipts. The human-control loop is request, visible plan, honest progress, evidence, bounded proposal, accessible decision, authoritative action, receipt, and recovery. Every transition has an owner, state, version, expiry, allowed actor, failure behavior, and user-facing explanation. The learning loop is outcome, diagram, alt text, explanation, trace, analogy, dual-stack mapping, case study, lab, checkpoint, glossary, sources, and progress. The same structured content model produces the document, website, search, and offline pack. Cross-cutting controls include tenant isolation, least privilege, schema validation, safe rendering, CSP and sandboxing, data minimization, consent and memory scope, accessibility, event and business audit, evaluation, incident recovery, attention policy, source freshness, and deletion verification.
trace: Maya opens a customer case and requests a refund-policy review with a named outcome, constraints, and privacy scope.
A coordinator delegates bounded research through A2A, reaches approved evidence and tools through MCP, and streams typed AG-UI state into the workspace.
RAG returns versioned evidence; an A2UI or MCP App surface may present an approved component view without receiving unrestricted code or host access.
Acme creates a proposal bound to current evidence, policy, amount, customer, actor, expiry, and recovery; Maya reviews and decides accessibly.
The authoritative action returns a receipt, partial or failed work remains visible, evaluation and privacy-minimized analytics record the outcome, and related visual lessons explain every layer.
lessons.analogy: An airport combines flight operations and a passenger information system. The engines, control tower, gates, signs, staff, security, accessibility services, and training must share truth without giving every part the same authority.
nextjs: Create route groups for workspace, tasks, artifacts, approvals, learning, search, privacy, and settings; keep privileged data server-side and isolate live or device behavior in narrow client components.
Implement one typed product-event adapter and reducer, one approved generated-component catalog, one sandboxed MCP App host, and one semantic visual-lesson renderer.
Build accessible state fixtures for every stage, partial success, conflict, approval, expiry, recovery, offline mode, privacy choice, and security block before connecting live services.
python: Define Pydantic contracts for tasks, events, evidence, proposals, decisions, tool intents, artifacts, receipts, lessons, consent, memory, notifications, feedback, and deletions.
Separate authoritative business records from event projections; coordinate durable work and compensation while adapting MCP, A2A, AG-UI, and A2UI versions at explicit boundaries.
Ship deterministic simulators and end-to-end fixtures first, then add providers behind interfaces with contract, policy, security, replay, accessibility-state, and evaluation tests.

caseStudy.situation: Maya reviews an urgent refund exception while the current policy conflicts with a stale retrieved copy and a third-party app proposes an unsafe custom approval surface.
walkthrough: The evidence freshness rule marks the stale copy as superseded and blocks the proposal from becoming actionable.
The generated UI validator rejects the unapproved component and the sandboxed app cannot call a host approval method without capability, consent, and server policy.
Acme preserves completed research, retrieves the current policy, replans the comparison, and presents a native accessible approval card bound to the new evidence version.
Maya approves the bounded exception; the server commits once, returns a receipt, updates the task, and links the relevant security, RAG, approval, and recovery lessons.
caseStudy.result: The system completes useful work while stale evidence and unsafe interface code fail closed without erasing progress or confusing Maya.
caseStudy.danger: A demo can appear full-stack while hiding the exact boundaries that matter: authoritative state, protocol versions, identity, policy, consent, accessibility, data deletion, and recovery after uncertain effects.
caseStudy.takeaway: Build one observable human-control system and two understandable experiences; protocols connect parts, but product contracts make them safe and teachable.

lessons.lab: Write the capstone design package: context and trust diagrams, domain and event models, task states and sequences, component and approval contracts, APIs, storage and deletion, accessibility, threats, evaluation, notifications, offline behavior, deployment, thirty acceptance tests, and a phased Next.js plus FastAPI backlog. Do not write production code yet.
lessons.checkpoint: Which protocol is the source of truth for whether the refund actually committed?
lessons.answer: None by itself. The authoritative Acme business system and its idempotent receipt establish the committed effect. MCP, A2A, AG-UI, and A2UI carry tools, tasks, interface events, or views around that truth.
glossary: Human-control loop - visible sequence from request through decision, effect, receipt, and recovery
Product contract - owned rule for state, authority, data, and behavior
Capstone - integrated design demonstrating the complete course
